title: Charts Tell Stories
bigIdea: A chart is a story of price over time, and the time range changes the story.

steps.prompt: Same stock, two charts: one shows a single day, the other shows five years. Which one is more likely to look scary?

options.text: The one-day chart, where small moves look huge
The five-year chart, which hides every move
They always look exactly the same

steps.reveal: Zoomed into one day, tiny moves fill the whole screen and look dramatic. Zoomed out to five years, the same wiggle barely shows.

cards.title: A line chart
cards.body: A line chart connects prices over time. Left is older, right is newer. The line's path is the story.

cards.title: Time ranges
cards.body: You can view one day, one month, one year, or more. Each range answers a different question about the stock.

cards.title: Zooming out
cards.body: Zooming out shows the bigger trend and calms down day-to-day noise. Neither view predicts the future.

steps.prompt: Match each anonymized chart shape to the headline that most likely goes with it. (Simulation; these are sample stories, not real companies.)

buckets.label: Chart: flat, then a sharp spike

items.text: Company grows sales steadily for years
Surprise bad news hits in a single day
Quiet for months, then a sudden breakthrough
Traders argue back and forth with no clear direction

steps.explanation: The chart's shape mirrors the story: steady growth climbs, a shock drops sharply, a breakthrough spikes after calm, and uncertainty looks choppy.

steps.prompt: A friend says a stock "looks terrifying" after seeing only its one-day chart. What is the best advice?

options.text: Zoom out to a longer range to see the bigger picture before judging
Trust the one-day chart; it predicts the future
Ignore charts entirely, they never mean anything

steps.explanation: The time range shapes the story. Zooming out to a longer range gives context that a single day cannot.
